subject: health
title: Application or project: public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak
focus: public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak
essentialQuestion: Why is health so unevenly distributed across places that are only a few miles apart?
keyPoints: Public health functions include surveillance, communication, prevention, testing support, coordination, and policy; outbreak response changes as evidence changes.
A defensible community response uses accurate data, identifies the actor with authority, proposes a feasible change, protects privacy and access, and defines how progress will be measured.

For public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Analyze a fictional community health dataset, identify the two conditions with the largest effect, and write a short brief proposing one realistic intervention with its likely limits.
studentTask: Draft a one-page fictional community response about public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak: state the condition with two facts, identify who has authority to act, propose one feasible change, name a privacy or access safeguard, and define one measure that would show progress.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Analysis may be written, charted, spoken, or completed on a supplied guided-analysis frame with the dataset pre-summarized.
extensionChallenge: Apply public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
Analysis may be written, charted, spoken, or completed on a supplied guided-analysis frame with the dataset pre-summarized.
trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Explain public health functions and how a community responds to an outbreak accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
